_: MACHINE STATE. OBSERVATION.md is generated from this file and is not authoritative. tools/sample.py reads survey_end_utc from here.
question: Which venue offers the cheapest-to-measure base rates per unit of effort? No a-priori answer exists, so it is bought with a one-week survey scored on weights fixed before the data.

outcome_definitions.death_class: reserve_in_usd < 0.05 x observed peak within 72h of first observation, or pool 404s on individual re-query
outcome_definitions.survivor_class: at day 14: reserve_in_usd >= 0.50 x observed peak AND >= venue median launch reserve_in_usd across all committed cohorts
outcome_definitions.unmeasurable: fetch error; never folded into either outcome

excluded_by_construction: any venue requiring paid data before H1 passes
known_limits: 3 pages x 20 pools per snapshot is a thin sample of a firehose; adequate for base rates and ranking, not for coverage.
8 divides 24, so every sample lands at the same three clock times: this cancels for cross-network ranking but biases absolute base rates; H1 cadence must correct it.
GeckoTerminal free tier is an unverified dependency; 429s were observed 2026-08-18 and the sampler now paces at 2.5s.
Peak is the max observed across snapshots, so it is an underestimate: the death test under-counts deaths rather than inflating them.
